stem: Which `plot_state_city` figure does this code produce?
code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.quantum_info import Statevector
from qiskit.visualization import plot_state_city

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.s(1)

plot_state_city(Statevector(qc))

A.alt: City plot of a two-qubit density matrix: the real-part panel carries two bars of height 0.5 on the |00><00| and |11><11| diagonal cells; the imaginary-part panel carries two off-diagonal bars, positive on the |00><11| cell and negative on the |11><00| cell.

B.alt: City plot of a two-qubit density matrix: the real-part panel carries two bars of height 0.5 on the |00><00| and |11><11| diagonal cells; the imaginary-part panel carries two off-diagonal bars, negative on the |00><11| cell and positive on the |11><00| cell.

C.alt: City plot of a two-qubit density matrix: the real-part panel carries two diagonal bars of height 0.5 plus two negative off-diagonal bars on the |00><11| and |11><00| cells; the imaginary-part panel is flat.

D.alt: City plot of a two-qubit density matrix: half of the sixteen cells of the real-part panel carry a bar of magnitude 0.25 and the rest are flat, and the imaginary-part panel is filled in the complementary pattern with bars of the same magnitude.

E.alt: City plot of a two-qubit density matrix: the real-part panel carries two diagonal bars of height 0.5 plus two positive off-diagonal bars on the |00><11| and |11><00| cells; the imaginary-part panel is flat.

explanation.correct: A city plot draws the density matrix: the left panel is its real part, the right panel its imaginary part. `h(0)` and `cx(0, 1)` build (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2), and `s(1)` multiplies the |11> amplitude by i, giving (|00> + i|11>)/sqrt(2). The populations stay at 0.5 on the |00> and |11> diagonal cells, but the coherence moves out of the real panel: rho[|00><11|] = -0.5i and rho[|11><00|] = +0.5i, so the imaginary panel gains the two off-diagonal bars with those signs.

distractors.A: S versus S-dagger: `sdg` would multiply the |11> amplitude by -i, which flips the sign of both imaginary off-diagonal bars relative to the drawing this code produces.
distractors.C: `s` is a quarter turn, not a half turn: `z` would multiply |11> by -1, keeping the coherence real and negative and leaving the imaginary panel flat.
distractors.D: Entanglement dropped: replacing `cx` with a second `h` gives a product state, whose density matrix has a bar in every one of the sixteen cells instead of only on the |00>/|11> block.
distractors.E: Treats the phase gate as unobservable: without `s` the coherence stays real and positive, so the imaginary panel would be flat. The phase here is relative, not global, so it does show up.

provenance.notes: Image-option item. The five option figures are plot_state_city renders of exactly the five states the proof builds; the proof compares the drawn density matrices cell by cell. plot_state_city uses mplot3d, hence platform_sensitive.
